summary_for_children: Al-'Ankabut means The Spider. It teaches that faith is tested, and that relying on anything besides Allah is like the spider's home, the weakest of homes. It mentions Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut and others.
environment_concept: A huge, fine spider's web (29:41), a road through many landscapes (29:20) and an ark resting on a ridge as a sign (29:15).
architecture_and_scenery: Rock and timber houses, a vast dew-covered web between trees, an ark on a ridge, and a long road through changing lands.

palette.lighting: Morning dew catching the light on the web

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Spider's House
story_library.children_narration: Everyone experiences challenges, and faith is tested through our choices. The Quran gives the example of the spider's house when describing how weak it is to rely on false protectors instead of Allah. The surah also recalls the stories of Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, and other communities.

world_idea.title: The Web of Choices
world_idea.description: Explore a giant artistic spider-web environment and test how different materials behave. Then visit narrative stations about faith and perseverance. Do not portray the spider's house as literally the weakest structure in all scientific respects.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
